Marcus / team — quick technical notes to inform the checklist: 

1) HSM profile and attestation
- We support AWS CloudHSM and on-prem Thales/HSM appliances; for staging we can provision a CloudHSM cluster with FIPS 140-2 validated modules and supply the attestation bundle.

2) Entropy / seed handling
- Option A: Customer-provided seed (Helix imports seed material via an HSM import session). The HSM will generate an import log that we can attach to the ceremony evidence.
- Option B: HSM-generated seed; Redwood records an HSM attestation of RNG health and provides the signed artifact.
- We recommend Option A for Helix if you want provenance under your custody. Note: if you import, the import is done over an admin session with dual control.

3) Operator eviction & zeroization steps (high level)
- Initiate eviction via a signed API call from Helix's ops account -> triggers operator hold timer (configurable, default 30m).
- After hold period, automated zeroize job runs on the operator node and HSM key handles are scheduled for eviction.
- System emits a ZeroizeReceipt (signed) plus a full audit bundle (syslogs, k8s events, calls to KMS).

4) Evidence and exports
- We can provide: Signed ZeroizeReceipt, HSM import logs, operator command logs, and a signed timeline for key roll (RFC-style).

5) Split custody pattern
- We support wrapping a master KEK with a split-wrapping scheme (2-of-3) where Helix holds one fragment and Redwood holds the other fragments. Offsite retention by Helix is recommended.

I'll convert this into a short technical checklist and create a rehearsal runbook. Any constraints on time zones or blackout windows for your engineering team?

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park\Security Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
